maya: heads up folks — ran the Python quickstart after accepting SSO invite and the UI shows a generic 'Request failed (403)'. CLI sample (python sdk) prints a different error: `Payment setup pending` while the browser just shows 403.

maya: network inspector shows two responses for the same operation: browser fetch -> 403 body: `{"error":"forbidden","message":"Request failed (403)"}`; python SDK -> 200 with body `{"status":"queued","detail":"payment_setup_in_progress"}` which the SDK maps to a friendly message. Confusing for new users.

onboard-bot: Hi @maya — new workspaces that recently added billing may have a short processing window. If billing is still provisioning, you may see a transient gating response. Add or verify billing here: https://console.redwood.ai/workspaces/demo123/billing :credit_card:

owen: interesting. Do you know whether the browser flow used the OIDC cookie and the SDK used a service key? That could explain different code paths.

maya: browser flow was browser-OAuth (no service key). The quickstart's client fetch hits the hosted API which currently returns a plain 403 for that condition. The Python SDK speaks to a different internal route that returns an explicit `payment_setup_in_progress` status which we display as a helpful message.

peter: short-term fix: map the 403 in the web quickstart to the same friendly copy as the SDK when we detect the `payment_setup_in_progress` condition. We could either (A) have the API include a machine-readable header `x-redwood-status: payment_setup_in_progress` on the 403, or (B) standardize the 403 body to include `code: payment_setup_in_progress`.

maya: +1. Also the quickstart README should mention a small window (1-3 minutes) after adding billing where requests may be rejected; recommend a retry button. New users are confused when one sample (python) looks OK and the browser one fails.

owen: another note: SDK parity issue — our Node and Python SDKs already surface `payment_setup_in_progress` as an exception type. JS quickstart (browser) needs the same UX so parity matches. Filing tiny tasks: SDK-112 (add parity doc), STUB-47 (quickstart banner + retry).

sdk-bot: Created SDK-112: "document payment_setup_in_progress mapping across SDKs" assigned to @peter.

peter: quick developers' workaround: run the quickstart with a service key env var for local dev (export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_xxx) so you bypass the provisioning gating. Also after attaching billing, wait ~30s and hit retry.

maya: confirmed service key works and unblocks local dev. I'll add a one-liner to the quickstart README and file a tiny docs PR describing the timing expectations.

owen: infra follow-up: I'll add `x-redwood-status: payment_setup_in_progress` header on 403 responses for the next rollout so clients can map without parsing bodies. INF-1401 opened.

peter: I'll push a micro-PR to the web quickstart to show a persistent banner when the header or body indicates billing provisioning; banner will include Console link + Retry button that polls `/v1/health` for 20s. ETA tomorrow.

maya: thanks — leaving this open until PRs and infra ticket land. This one should reduce a lot of first-call confusion. :thumbsup:
